t: For carrying out the provisions of titles I, II, and III of the Vocational Education Act or 1946, as amended (20 U.S.C. 15i–15m, 15o–15q, 15aa–15jj, 15aaa–15ggg), section 1 of the Act of March 3, 1931 (20 U.S.C. 30), the Act of March 18, 1950 (20 U.S.C. 31–33), section 9 of the Act of August 1, 1956 (20 U.S.C. 34), section 2 of the Act of September 25, 1962 (48 U.S.C. 1667), section 9 of the National Vocational Student Loan Insurance Act of 1965 (74 Stat. 1037, 1041), and the Vocational Education Act of 1963 (except sections 4(c), 13 and 14) (20 U.S.C. 35C(c), 35(k) and 35(1)); $252,900,000, of which $199,309,000 shall be for vocational education programs under section 4(a) and (b) of the Vocational Education Act of 1963 (20 U.S.C. 35C(a) and (b)), and $3,600,000 to remain available until expended shall be for interest payments on insured loans under the National Vocational Student Loan Insurance Act of 1965; and, in addition, $10,000,000 for work-study programs under section 13 of the Vocational Education Act of 1963 to be derived by transfer from funds available to the Office of Economic Opportunity for fiscal year 1968.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriations provision that funds vocational education programs and transfers money from the Office of Economic Opportunity. The tempting reading is that references to vocational education programs and state-administered acts imply coordination with states, but the text only sets dollar amounts and their sources. It requires no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: $252,900,000, of which $199,309,000 shall be for vocational education programs under section 4(a) and (b) of the Vocational Education Act of 1963

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that allocates specific dollar amounts for various vocational education programs and loan interest payments. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. It merely authorizes the spending of funds.
qwen_block.s: For carrying out the provisions of titles I, II, and III of the Vocational Education Act or 1946... $252,900,000... shall be for vocational education programs... and $3,600,000... shall be for interest payments on insured loans... and, in addition, $10,000,000 for work-study programs... to be derived by transfer from funds available to the Office of Economic Opportunity

opus.w: This is a plain appropriation. It sets aside money for vocational education programs, interest payments on insured student loans, and work-study programs, including a transfer from the Office of Economic Opportunity. One might be tempted to read the references to loans and work-study as outside involvement. But receiving benefits or funds is not taking part in a federal decision, and nothing here calls for consultation, hearings, advisory bodies, rulemaking, or a right to sue.
opus.s: $252,900,000, of which $199,309,000 shall be for vocational education programs under section 4(a) and (b) of the Vocational Education Act of 1963

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the expenditure of funds for various vocational education programs. It does not establish a mechanism for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before making a decision. The mention of work-study programs refers to the use of funds, not a participatory decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: For carrying out the provisions of titles I, II, and III of the Vocational Education Act or 1946, as amended... $252,900,000... and, in addition, $10,000,000 for work-study programs under section 13 of the Vocational Education Act of 1963 to be derived by transfer from funds available to the Office of Economic Opportunity for fiscal year 1968.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it mentions "work-study programs" and "vocational education," which involve students and workers.
Resolution: This is an appropriations clause that authorizes the spending of funds. It does not describe a process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties before making a decision; it simply allocates money for existing programs.
